feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the positioning is clear, the career progression is logical, and the experience aligns well with the headline. It reads professionally, but it would be more impactful with tighter consolidation of overlapping skills sections and more outcome-focused achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative: the summary, title, and progression at NACo strongly support a Digital Communications & Strategy Lead profile.  
- Good credibility and specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Microsoft Clarity, and the 10,000+ page migration add substance and technical depth.  
- Writing is generally polished and concise, with strong action verbs and a consistent professional tone.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than impact. Include measurable outcomes where possible (engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance, cost savings).  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with one or two concrete differentiators and slightly less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Add a clearer senior-value statement tied to recent work, e.g. enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and analytics-driven communications.
- Tighten the list of channels so it reads less like a skills inventory and more like a positioning summary.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, digital governance, and workflow design that improves coordination, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid adding specific tools here; those are already well covered elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if it emphasized higher-level capabilities and used more parallel, polished phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize wording for parallel structure: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial workflow & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process design • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Replace “Multi-channel communication” with “Cross-channel communications” for more natural phrasing and consistency with the header.
- Consider elevating “Web & CMS administration” to “Web platform & CMS management” to sound more strategic and senior.
- Pair related items where possible, e.g., “Editorial workflow & governance” and “Analytics, reporting & optimization,” to add specificity without adding length.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; avoid listing tools or overly detailed technical items here.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills; keep this block focused on strategic competencies.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, web modernization, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper impact statements, e.g.:
- “Built cross-functional digital workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and user discovery experience.”
- Replace task phrasing like “deliver” and “advise” with stronger verbs: led, built, designed, streamlined, launched.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, publishing teams enabled, traffic, engagement, search success, or time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new or more advanced here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, video production, and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Combine the first two bullets and lead with the website outcome: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused; add metrics if available: email open/click rates, audience growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten remaining bullets to action + result: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video series”; “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-programming language may duplicate the older NACo video bullets unless framed here as scale/build-out leadership.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems point: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and improved digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped improve” is too soft and repeats the governance/workflow language used in the Director role.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/workflow automation.
- Remove lower-signal platforms unless central to target roles; consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here and leaving them in “Technical + IT.”
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to echo the 10,000+ page migration without repeating full metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats Core Competencies; keep it in only one topline area if space is tight.

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:

items.title: University of Virginia

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform, give it clearer prominence.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling depth: “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just names: “CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Keep this item platform-only; avoid adding modernization, APIs, or AI language here since those are already covered elsewhere.
- If you want more impact, replace GitHub Pages with a stronger platform/tool only if it reflects meaningful recent use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the Topline Skills item “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages.
- Consider merging or trimming one of the two sections to avoid repeating the same platform list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and, where possible, reflect current/recent tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied capability, e.g. “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)”
- Consider grouping by function for scannability: “Front-end: HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery | Integrations: APIs, GTM | Deployment/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, replace older/general items with more current specifics tied to recent work, e.g. Drupal front-end theming, CMS troubleshooting, search implementation, or analytics tagging.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; keep this item strictly technical/build-oriented to avoid repetition.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by strongest/most relevant tools first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider replacing 1–2 generic collaboration apps with higher-signal specifics or integrations used at scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack” and “Teams” are low-impact on their own; they can dilute the section unless grouped as collaboration tools.
- Avoid repeating “workflow automation” language elsewhere; let this section show tools, while experience bullets show outcomes.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since the CV already proves email leadership in recent roles, this item should be tightened and framed around enterprise email/member engagement systems rather than repeating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light context: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, and member engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Keep only the strongest/recent tools; if one was used minimally, remove it rather than listing everything.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding phrases like “managed newsletters” here.
- “Engagement” may also blur with analytics/communications competencies, so keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup for later NACo roles rather than a distinct accomplishment entry. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables: website refresh support, livestream production, weekly video series, editorial/distribution support.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time improvements.
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update, and provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete ownership and outputs, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles at NACo.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and lead with action/result: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with something more specific, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience/stakeholder reach, or types of projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital communications” language that overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Associate Director roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; save management/growth language for the more senior NACo entries.
